correctness.rationale: TARGET route: prove-direction claim of small-time local approximate controllability with explicit (T*,delta,q,C)=(0.1,0.02,12,1e6) is not established. Analytically correct fragments (simplicity/parity/selection rule, commutators [H0,x]=-2ip, Gram invertibility form) do not compose into the headline. Fatal gaps: (1) First-order Duhamel/moment analysis with ||u||<=C T^-q leaves nonlinear remainder O(||u||^2 T)=O(T^{-2q+1}) diverging as T->0, never bounded; larger budget does not imply achievability. (2) Impulsive kick K(a)=exp(-iax) via large pulse ignores H0 drift with unbounded H0 and unbounded x; no Trotter/commutator error uniform on D(H0)-ball. (3) Finite N-mode Lie-rank/Hermes-Kawski invocation does not transfer to infinite-dimensional unbounded-drift PDE; truncation breaks commutators, nearest-coupling growth and 9% off-tridiagonal leakage unaddressed, even-mode cascade cost unproved. (4) Tail estimate only for e^{-iax}phi0 at N=6, not for targets uniformly nor for trajectories pumped by large controls; compactness of target ball does not control driven high-mode excitation. (5) Strict gap increase, nonzero couplings, Gram exponents, steering demo are mesh-converged FD numerics (L=8,h=0.01) and linear moment solves only, explicitly admitted as non-interval evidence; no full nonlinear Schrodinger steering simulation. Proof versus experimental evidence is therefore conflated. This is a correctness/evidence defect, not a bounded presentation fix.

value.rationale: Under TARGET policy and shared STANDARD, the headline if proved would be independently worth retrieving: small-time locally approximate controllability with explicit polynomial cost for the natural anharmonic x^2+x^4 dipole system addresses a recognized hard benchmark in bilinear Schrodinger control (small-time versus large-time, minimal-time obstructions, return method, non-resonant spectrum), motivated before computation. It is not a textbook restatement, mere parameter substitution, tiny unmotivated gain, or unexplained enumeration; explicit (T*,delta,q,C) are illustrative sufficient constants for a concrete theorem form, and a future researcher could need the precise small-time polynomial-cost fact. No ADMISSION_DEFECT is exposed; value is judged on the strongest self-contained headline separate from the incomplete surrounding numerics. Hence value PASSES even though correctness FAILS.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader theorems do not subsume the submitted single-input quartic-dipole small-time polynomial-cost claim: large-time results lack the arbitrarily-small-T plus C T^-q qualifier, and small-time diffeomorphism results require richer control action than multiplication by x alone (linear phases only) and different free Hamiltonians. Hypotheses compared literally, not by title similarity, so no dominance coverage.

Submitted conclusion: for H0=-dxx+x^2+x^4, B=x, every D(H0) delta-neighbour of ground orbit reachable within L2 delta/2 in every T<=0.1 with cost <=1e6 T^-12.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: No prior conclusion logically implies the submitted time-cost qualifier for this operator pair: large-time does not imply small-time polynomial cost, torus/R^d multi-control sufficiency does not imply single-dipole quartic sufficiency, and a necessary obstruction does not imply sufficiency. The DRAFT's linear moment-scaling polynomial observation is compatibility evidence, not implication of full nonlinear small-time controllability.
